A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LV-MAE with matching authors, methods, and main experiments. The complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables, and figures, support comparison; relocated and renumbered content can be matched.

before.justification: V1 reports original LV-MAE results on LVU, Breakfast, and COIN, component ablations, and qualitative reconstruction experiments in the main text and appendix.

after.justification: V2 retains those original results and adds segmentation, temporal-coverage, and feature-extractor experiments, plus Kinetics-400/600 evaluation.

M1.justification: The frozen short-video encoders, masked-embedding encoder-decoder, MSE objective, masking strategies, padding, and downstream probing procedures remain unchanged. The additional segmentation and feature-extractor variants are experimental ablations rather than replacements for the proposed method.

E1.justification: Appendix 10 adds short-video action-recognition evaluation on Kinetics-400 and Kinetics-600, previously mentioned only in connection with prior methods' training. The original pre-training sources, three main benchmarks, and movie-caption retrieval setting remain.

E2.justification: V2 Table 10 adds an evaluated LV-MAE variant using a frame-MAE feature extractor. Its other comparison methods and scores already occur in v1 Table 1, and the comparator sets in Tables 1–2 are unchanged. CoSeg is discussed but not evaluated.

E3.justification: Appendix 9 introduces substantial controlled variations: 10- and 15-second segments, shot-based segmentation, overlapping five-second segments, a five-minute training-clip cap, and varying input-frame counts. Section 4.4 also introduces R@5 reporting. These supplement the existing experiments; the original training and probing settings in Tables 5–7 remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V1 tests probing, masking strategy and ratio, and encoder depth. V2 substantially extends this analysis to segmentation sensitivity, overlap, training-video duration, input-frame coverage, and frame-MAE versus clip-level features. Much of Table 10 repeats existing architecture comparisons, but its feature-extractor control and the temporal analyses are new.

E5.justification: Neither version reports random seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or statistical significance tests. The additional results continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 and 8 retain their values, but substantial new results appear. LVU scores include 61.43/61.05/62.17 for 10-second/15-second/shot segments, 58.90 with overlap, 55.58 with the five-minute training cap, and 54.3 with frame-MAE features. Figure 5 adds the frame-count trend. V2 also reports retrieval R@5 of 75.34% and K400/K600 accuracy of 78.2%/79.1%, alongside LanguageBind's 77.6%/79.5%. These are added results, not revisions to existing benchmark scores.

T1.justification: The encoder, decoder, and loss formulations in Equations 1–3 are unchanged, and neither version develops theoretical proofs. V2 removes v1's displayed standard cosine-similarity formula while retaining cosine retrieval; this is an explanatory deletion rather than a mathematical change.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same central contributions: efficient masked-embedding learning for long videos, strong benchmark performance through probing, and caption-based interpretation. The rewritten conclusion preserves their scope; the additional experiments mainly support existing claims.

C2.justification: Appendix 9 newly attributes overlap degradation to redundant context, links increased frame coverage to better motion understanding, and argues that MAE training and extended temporal context are both important. Appendix 10 argues that short-video performance is preserved. The existing limitations concerning frozen embeddings and approximate interpretability remain.

D1.justification: V2's abstract adds a code-repository address and states that code is available. Appendix 9 additionally states that compared methods use identical input resolution. Existing architectural details, hardware and training-time disclosures, and hyperparameter tables are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds CoSeg and acknowledges its decoupling strategy, distinguishing LV-MAE through clip-level rather than frame-level representations. The remaining cited works and broader research positioning are retained despite reference renumbering.

P1.justification: V2 corrects several typos, condenses explanatory paragraphs and the conclusion, and makes appendix cross-references explicit. It expands Appendix 9 and inserts a short-video performance section, while retaining most wording and the overall organization.

P2.justification: V2 adds Tables 9–10 and a frame-count plot as Figure 5. Table 10 largely redisplays selected Table 1 results with one new variant. The previous appendix Figure 5 is preserved as Figure 6; existing displays retain their structure apart from minor formatting and page reflow.

improvement.justification: The new segmentation and temporal-coverage controls provide useful evidence for design choices that v1 left untested, while code-access information and the CoSeg discussion improve reproducibility documentation and positioning. The gains remain limited by terse new experimental protocols and unchanged uncertainty reporting. V2 also retains a stale statement describing the now-reported 10–15-second segment experiments as future work. Overall, these additions strengthen the existing study without substantially transforming its quality.
